newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-P&U shares drop as downgrades seen.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-P&U shares drop as downgrades seen.

text.p: U.S./Swedish drugs company Pharmacia & Upjohn (P&U) on Wednesday reported 1996 results as expected but analysts said fears over currency and product launch costs sent its shares lower.
Most analysts said they expected to lower their forecasts for earnings per share in 1997 and 1998 after the company injected a note of caution into its outlook.
"The long-term story is intact but the outlook for earnings in 1997 and 1998 is less encouraging than it was yesterday," Paribas analyst John Reeve said.
"This is mainly because the company is more cautious on the currency outlook than in November and is talking about greater costs behind new product launches than previously anticipated."
Reeve said he expected to lower his earnings per share forecast for 1997 to $2.15 from $2.25 and for 1998 by 10 cents to $2.50.
Results for 1996 were in line with expectations.

After a rollercoaster year with the shock departure of chief executive John Zabriskie, the company reported a 6.1 percent rise in earnings per share (EPS) to $1.90 on net earnings of $998 million. The market had expected EPS of $1.92.
The report initially calmed market nerves and P&U shares rose by six crowns.

But volatility quickly set in and this was not helped by company comments that it might not meet its goal of a 25 percent operating profit margin by 1998, up from 19.8 percent in 1996. Shares closed seven crowns lower at 275 crowns.
"The 1996 numbers were fair enough but then the company ran into one or two adverse factors," Dresdner Kleinwort Benson analyst Stephen Putnam said.

"We expect to have a 10 cents EPS downgrade for 1997 (to $2.15), of which half can be attributed to currency issues and the other five cents to the drug development programme being ahead of schedule, which will bring additional costs this year."
New York analyst David Maris from Aros Securities said there were concerns over the quality of products in the pipeline.
"The P&U story right now is a balance between concerns over quality and an already relatively discounted valuation," Maris said.
Aros Securities has for six months had a "reduce" trading recommendation on P&U, the product of a merger of U.S. group Upjohn Co and Sweden's Pharmacia AB in November 1995.
Putnam said Dresdner Kleinwort Benson would retain a "buy" recommendation on the stock with P&U expected to show 13 percent earnings growth in 1997.
"We think they are a buy because the shares are at a 30 percent discount to the peer group," Putnam said.
Reeve said the long-term trading recommendation by Paribas was positive but requiring no action in the short term.
"I think in terms of sales growth P&U is still slower than the industry average," Reeve said.
P&U posted a 3.3 percent rise in net sales in 1996 to $7.18 billion, saying sales were driven by new-product performance and marketing synergies.
"Our focus in 1997 will be to build and consolidate our position to generate longer-term strong performance," P&U's chief executive Jan Ekberg said in a statement.
"We will concentrate on investing in new-product introductions, some of which are coming sooner than anticipated."
